questions.stem: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes. After one complete round of mitosis, how many chromosomes will each daughter cell have?
questions.explanation: Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells, each with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell (46). A common misconception is confusing mitosis with meiosis -- meiosis halves the chromosome number to 23, but mitosis keeps it the same.

questions.stem: A scientist observes that a drug prevents chromosomes from being pulled apart during cell division. At which stage of mitosis would cell division be blocked?

options.text: Anaphase, when chromosomes are separated by spindle fibres

questions.explanation: During anaphase, spindle fibres contract to pull the sister chromatids apart to opposite poles of the cell. If the chromosomes cannot be pulled apart, the cell would be stuck at anaphase. This is actually how some anti-cancer drugs work -- by disrupting spindle formation to prevent cancer cells dividing.

questions.stem: A wound on a patient's skin heals over several days as new skin cells are produced. Which type of cell division is responsible for this healing?

options.text: Meiosis, to produce diverse replacement cells
Mitosis, to produce identical replacement cells

questions.explanation: Wound healing requires the production of new cells that are genetically identical to the existing skin cells. Mitosis produces two identical daughter cells from each parent cell, making it the correct division type for growth and repair. Meiosis only occurs in reproductive organs to make gametes.

questions.stem: Under a microscope, a student counts 100 cells in a root tip sample. 10 cells are in the process of mitosis. What percentage of the cell cycle is spent in mitosis?
questions.explanation: If 10 out of 100 cells are undergoing mitosis, this suggests approximately 10% of the cell cycle is spent in mitosis. This is a common practical where the mitotic index (proportion of cells in mitosis) is calculated. Most of the cell cycle is actually spent in interphase (about 90%).

questions.stem: Strawberry plants can reproduce asexually by sending out runners. The new plants are genetically identical to the parent. Which type of cell division produces the cells of the runners?

options.text: A combination of mitosis and meiosis

questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction in plants (such as runners in strawberries) relies on mitosis, which produces genetically identical cells. This is why the offspring are clones of the parent plant. Meiosis would introduce genetic variation, and binary fission only occurs in prokaryotes.
